paper.title: Learning-to-Defer in Non-Stationary Time Series via Switching State-Space Models

settings.name_in_paper: Learning-to-defer in non-stationary time series with selective (bandit) expert feedback and historical full-feedback archive
unmapped: Actions are the internal forecast (action 0) or one of K experts; costs are squared forecast error plus known fees beta_k, bounded by C_* = 4B^2 + beta_max (rescaled to [0,1])
Target y_t is always observed, so the internal action's cost is always revealed; consulting expert k reveals only expert k's forecast (feedback graph: every action observes itself and action 0)
Targets, forecasts, contexts and availabilities come from an arbitrary unknown (possibly non-stationary, history-dependent) law; no i.i.d. assumption, and no variation budget is used
A historical archive with full feedback on all experts is available before deployment (fitting and calibration segments)
The learner knows the fees beta_k and the output bound B
settings.definition_quote: At round $t$, the system observes context $\vect{x}_t\in\mathcal X$ and the available external experts $\mathcal E_t\subseteq\{1,\ldots,K\}$. It produces an internal forecast $f_t$ and chooses $I_t$ from $\mathcal A_t=\{0\}\cup\mathcal E_t$. ... The target $y_t$ is observed after the forecast interval, whereas an external forecast is observed only when it is selected.

algorithms.name: L2D-SLDS (greedy routing with moment-score weighted SLDS candidates)

symbols.B_T: predictive-moment budget min_j {2 log(1/w_{1,j}) + E sum_t Delta_{t,j}}
symbols.Xi_T: E sum_t xi_t, cumulative cost-contrast residual
symbols.B_out: bound on targets and forecasts, values in (-B,B)

conditions: Observable cost contrasts (Assumption 1) holds almost surely with deterministic Lambda and predictable xi_t
tuning: greedy argmin of aggregated predicted costs

source.label: thm:pr-main
source.quote: Under the protocol of Section~\ref{sec:pr-problem}, conditionally on the archive, and under the cost-contrast condition, \operatorname{Reg}_T(\varphi)\leq C_*\Lambda\sqrt{T\mathcal B_T/2} +C_*\Lambda\epsilon T/\sqrt2 +C_*\mathbb E\sum_t\xi_t+2B^2\mathcal B_T .

results.notes: Regret is against a per-round conditional-risk oracle with internal prediction varphi (any predictable varphi in [-B,B]). The environment/feedback mapping is approximate. The appendix shows that an exact candidate gives B_T <= 2 log(L/zeta) + 2 when epsilon = 1/(T+1).

symbols.S_kappa: sum_t sqrt(kappa_t), with kappa_t the chi^2 divergence bound of accurate candidates
symbols.S_b: sum_t bar b_t, with bar b_t = min{1, U exp(-(t-1) gamma_L^2/4)} and U = (L-1)e^{A/2}(e^{-N gamma_H^2/4} + L (zeta/(L(1-zeta)))^{1/4})

conditions: a nonempty set G of accurate candidates whose target and target-expert pair laws are within chi^2 divergence kappa_t of the truth (deterministic kappa_t)
total reference error over calibration and deployment at most A almost surely
every inaccurate candidate accumulates separation at least N gamma_H^2 over calibration and n gamma_L^2 over every live prefix of length n

source.label: thm:pr-archive-robust
source.quote: Under the protocol of Section~\ref{sec:pr-problem} and the preceding divergence, reference-error, and separation conditions, with deterministic $\kappa_t$ and exact predictive integration, \operatorname{Reg}_T(y^\star)\leq C_*\sum_t\sqrt{\kappa_t} +B^2\sum_t(\sqrt{\kappa_t}+\epsilon)^2 +(2C_*+4B^2)\sum_t\bar b_t . If these conditions hold jointly with fitting-conditioned probability at least $1-\delta$, the bound holds with an additional $C_*T\delta$.

results.notes: Comparator internal prediction is the Bayes prediction y^star. If the conditions hold only with probability 1-delta, the bound gains an additive term C_* T delta.

source.label: cor:pr-sublinear
source.quote: (i) If some candidate is exact and the cost-contrast condition holds with $\xi_t=0$, then for fixed $0<\zeta<1$, $\operatorname{Reg}_T(y^\star)=O\bigl(\sqrt{T\log(eL/\zeta)}\bigr)$.

results.notes: Follows from Theorem (thm:pr-main) with B_T <= 2 log(L/zeta) + 2.

conditions: every candidate in G satisfies kappa_t <= c/T in both phases, with c fixed
historical separation gamma_H > 0 fixed (live separation gamma_L may be 0)
N = Theta(log(T+1)) calibration dates, sufficiently many

source.label: cor:pr-sublinear
source.quote: (ii) If $L\geq2$, every candidate in $\mathcal G$ satisfies $\kappa_t\leq c/T$ in both phases, and $c$ and $\gamma_{\rm H}>0$ are fixed, then sufficiently many $N=\Theta(\log(T+1))$ calibration dates and a sufficiently small mixing weight $\zeta=O((T+1)^{-4})$ give $\operatorname{Reg}_T(y^\star)=O(\sqrt T)$, even when $\gamma_{\rm L}=0$.

results.notes: Explicit form in the appendix: Reg_T <= C_* T sqrt(kappa) + B^2 T (sqrt(kappa)+eps)^2 + 2C_* + 4B^2. If the certificate fails with probability delta, the bound gains C_* T delta, so the rate needs delta = O(T^-1/2).
